newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee eases grudgingly on RBI dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee eases grudgingly on RBI dlr buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee eased by a mere two paise against the dollar despite massive intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Tuesday, dealers said.
The chief dealer at a foreign bank said RBI must have bought over $200 million from the spot market on Tuesday.
"I don't know if it was that much," said a dealer at another leading bank. "It is certainly more than $150 million." Dealers said the RBI bought at several levels throughout the day.
The spot dollar closed at 35.9050/9150, down from 35.8750/8850 opening, dealers said.
The rupee saw a low of 35.91 on Tuesday, with some stray deals at 35.9150, dealers said. The day's high was 35.8750.

"It's hardly any movement," said a dealer, referring to the rupee's two paise movement against the backdrop of large RBI intervention. Two leading Indian financial institutions were also buying dollars on Tuesday, dealers said.
"I guess it was a concerted move to hammer the rupee down," said the chief forex dealer at a leading foreign bank.
Some dealers said the GDR proceeds of around $500 million raised by Indian overseas telecom monopoly Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) could increase the dollar supply in the local market.
Despite reports that VSNL's GDR money will enter the local market by March 31, most dealers said this may not happen.
"Most probably they (VSNL) will sell to SBI (State Bank of India, VSNL's banker) who will match it with their outflows," said a dealer. "I don't see it hitting the local market."
RBI continued to buy outright dollars in the forward market, but the level of forward intervention was modest in comparison to its intervention in the spot market, dealers said.
